[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Households (N)** = 8 + 7 + 3 + 8 + 4 = 30.

Total **Children** = (0 × 8) + (1 × 7) + (2 × 3) + (3 × 8) + (4 × 4) = 53.

**Mean** = 53 ÷ 30 = 1.7666...

**Median** (even N=30) = Average of 15th (value 1) and 16th (value 2) observation = 1.5.

**Difference** = 1.767 − 1.5 = 0.267 ≈ 0.27.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Frequency distribution of **number of children (x)** and **number of households (f)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96c378faa1b108731603f4d7d35041057d1d8d415de6142a80d8f06a724759f9.png] 

**Step 1: Calculate the Mean**

⇒ Mean (µ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ

⇒ Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) = (8 × 0) + (7 × 1) + (3 × 2) + (8 × 3) + (4 × 4)

⇒ Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) = 0 + 7 + 6 + 24 + 16 = 53

⇒ Total Households (N) = Σfᵢ = 30

⇒ Mean = 53 ÷ 30 = 1.7666... (recurring)

**Step 2: Calculate the Median**

Find cumulative frequencies (CF):

⇒ CF for x=0 is 8

⇒ CF for x=1 is 8 + 7 = 15

⇒ CF for x=2 is 15 + 3 = 18

⇒ Since N = 30 (even), Median = [Value at (N/2)th + Value at (N/2 + 1)th] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = [Value at 15th position + Value at 16th position] ÷ 2

⇒ From CF, 15th value is 1 and 16th value is 2.

⇒ Median = (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5

**Step 3: Calculate the Difference**

⇒ Difference = |Mean − Median|

⇒ Difference = |1.7666... − 1.5| = 0.2666...

⇒ Difference ≈ 0.27 (correct up to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 0.27.**

questions.question: Pipe V1 can fill an empty tank in 8 hours. Pipe V2 can fill the same tank in 16 hours. Pipe V3 can empty the same, completely filled, tank in 12 hours. If three pipes are opened simultaneously, then in how much time will the tank get completely filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe V1 can fill an empty tank in 8 hours.

Pipe V2 can fill the same tank in 16 hours.

Pipe V3 can empty the same completely filled tank in 12 hours.

Three pipes are opened simultaneously.

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by three different pipes = LCM of (a, b, c)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/b

Efficiency of third pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/c

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (+ efficiency of 2nd pipe) + (- efficiency of 3rd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a + 1/b - 1/c

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a + 1/b - 1/c) = abc/(bc + ac - ab) hours

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aea245b2b7472a0ca677825d546513b76d745cb40de2410b9b49ca9fbc43a81.png] 

In fig, LCM of (8, 16, 12) = 48 = Total work

Efficiency of V1 = 48/8 = 6

Efficiency of V2 = 48/16 = 3

Efficiency of V3 = 48/12 = 4

Combined efficiency = (+ 6) + (+ 3) + (- 4) = 5

**∴ If all three pipes open simultaneously, then the tank filled in = 48/5 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

V1 fills in 8 hours

V2 fills in 16 hours

V3 empties in 12 hours

So time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a + 1/b - 1/c) = 1/(1/8 + 1/16 - 1/12) = 1/(5/48) = 48/5 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 48/5 hours. **

questions.question: _________ is the highest gallantry award for officers and other enlisted personnel of all military branches of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __Param Vir Chakra__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The Gallantry Award is meant for exceptional courage, valour and dignity. In India, Gallantry award are given to the personnel of the forces for their exceptional bravery.
 
• After Independence, the three Gallantry awards came into force i.e. the Paramvir Chakra, the Mahavir Chakra and the Veer Chakra.
 
• The Gallantry awards are announced twice in a year i.e on Republic day and on Independence day.
 
• The order of Precedence of these awards is 

 
• Param Vir Chakra
 
• Ashoka Chakra
 
• Mahavir Chakra
 
• Kirti Chakra
 
• Vir Chakra
 
• Shaurya Chakra

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Param Vir Chakra:

 
• The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for most conspicuous bravery or some daring or pre-eminent act of valour or self-sacrifice, in the presence of the enemy, whether on land, at sea, or in the air.
 
• Param Vir Chakra means "Wheel of the Ultimate Brave".

Ashok Chakra:

 
• The Ashok Chakra is India's highest peacetime military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
 
• It is the peacetime equivalent of the Param Vir Chakra.

Kirti Chakra:

 
• The Kirti Chakra is an Indian military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the field of battle.
 
• It may be awarded to civilians as well as military personnel, including posthumous awards. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Maha Vir Chakra

Vir Chakra:

 
• Vir Chakra is an Indian gallantry award presented for acts of gallantry in the presence of the enemy on the battlefield.

questions.question: In which of the following type of organism autotrophic nutrition is found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bacteria.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The mode of nutrition in which organisms make food themselves from simple substances is called **autotrophic (auto = self; Trophos = nourishment) nutrition.**
 
• Some types of **bacteria are autotrophs.**
 
• Most autotrophs use a process called photosynthesis to make their food, like Algae, phytoplankton, and** some bacteria also perform photosynthesis.**
 
• Some bacteria make their own food by converting** light energy, chemical energy or inorganic substances into usable energy** that these single-celled organisms need to live. 
 
 
• Ex- Plants, Tress, algae, Bactria etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Mode of** Nutrition:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c2278aa152a6f8aac05d23f06b278d4c1e84822c8ba8f4474c0a5775dcd0213.png] 

 

 
• Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food, using materials from inorganic sources by using basic energy sources such as sunlight.

 
 
• Plants are the main example of autotrophs, using photosynthesis.
 
• Some autotrophs, such as green plants and algae, are phototrophs, they convert electromagnetic energy from sunlight into chemical energy in the form of glucose. So, Spinach, Tomato, Banana are also examples of autotrophs.
 
 
 
• Heterotrophic: Animals and most other organisms take in ready-made food prepared by the plants. They are called heterotrophs (heteros = other). 
 
 
• Examples are Protozoa, viruses, fungi etc.
